To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 1.3lambda-cavity oxide-confined GaIn(NAs)/GaAs-based VCSEL is the best lased device in terms of the RT CW lasing performance (the shortest lasing wavelength and the lowest threshold), while the 3lambda- cavity VCSEL is the better lasing design in terms of the lasing wavelength, single-mode lasing, and lasing performance (threshold) at high temperatures.

the lowest CW lasing threshold can be achieved in the intracavity-contact VCSEL with only one oxide-confined aperture (for smaller sizes) or with two oxide-confined apertures ( for larger sizes) and that the best design for the single-fundamentalmode operation with longer lasing wavelength is the intracavity contact VCSEL with one large aperture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the comparative analysis of RT CW lasing operation of various designs (1.5lambda, 3lambda, and 4lambda) of oxide-confined GaInNAs/GaAs quantum well VCSELs.
the comparative analysis of various designs of VCSELs, including the 3lambda- and 1.5 lambda-cavity VCSELs with one and two oxide aperturas.
a comparative analysis of various designs of GaIn(NAs)/GaAs oxide-confined VCSELS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 3lambda cavity design with one oxide aperture provides the best lasing characteristics for the 1.3-1.5mum GaIn(NAs)/GaAs-based VCSELs, especially when the active region is relatively large (i.e., 3.5 mu m or more).
the 1.3lambda-cavity and the 3lambda cavity VCSELs with only one oxide confinement layer are the most promising lasing designs of the oxide-confined VCSELS for RT CW operation.
, for the RT CW operation, the 3 lambda-cavity VCSELs with only one oxide confinement aperture are the best lasing devices for the 1.3-1.6-mum wavelength range.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the 1lambda-cavity oxide-confined VCSELS are the most suitable for the RT CW operation and the 3lambda ones are the best for the single-fundametal-mode lasing operation at RT. Proc. the 3lambda cavity with two oxide apetures is the best laseing design for the 1.3mum wavelength, the single fundamental mode operation and the low threshold operation, while the 1. 5lambda cavity with one oxide aperture and the 3lambda cavitiy with one oxide aperture are the best lase designs for the 1, 3mum wavelength and the low threshold, respectively.
the 3lambda- and 1.5lambdacavity oxide-confined VCSELS with one oxide aperture are the best lasing designs for the GaIn)(NAs)GaAs active region.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in general, the VCSEL design with one oxide aperture and the 3lambda cavity is the most suitable for the RT CW threshold operation, especially for the larger oxide apertures and the larger active regions.

, in order to achieve the best possible performance of the oxide-confined GaIn(NAs)/GaAs quantum-well VCSELs, one should take into account the influence of the cavity design, the number of oxide apertures and their sizes, and the active region size on the RT lasing characteristics.
, for a given oxide-aperture size and a given active-region size, the 1.3lambda- and 3lambda-cavities VCSELs with one oxide aperture have the lowest RT CW lased threshold.
